home.title: Browser-side AI models
home.modelsCount: {count} catalog entries · models, tools and applications
home.aboutTitle: Bring more AI tasks into the browser
home.aboutLead: The browser can be more than an entry point to an AI service: it can also run AI applications locally. With tools such as Transformers.js and ONNX Runtime Web, developers can bring text processing, image recognition and speech transcription to users’ devices, adding useful AI capabilities to web applications.
home.aboutBody: Local inference allows some tasks to process inputs without sending them to a remote model service. It can reduce network round trips and cloud inference costs, and support offline use once model resources are available. This project brings together models, tools and application ideas to help developers discover suitable browser AI tasks and integrate them into everyday web applications. Actual support depends on the model, browser and device.

categories.textDesc: Classical NLP tasks running locally in the browser.
categories.llmDesc: Large language models and code assistants on the web.
categories.search-ragDesc: Embedding, reranking and semantic retrieval in JavaScript.
categories.visionDesc: Classical computer vision: detection, segmentation, OCR, depth.
categories.generative-visionDesc: Text-to-image and inpainting models in the browser.
categories.audioDesc: Speech recognition, synthesis, denoising and source separation.
categories.generative-audioDesc: Text-to-music and voice cloning models running in the browser.
categories.multimodalDesc: Vision-language, CLIP and document understanding models.
categories.real-timeDesc: Perception tasks; real-time performance depends on device and configuration.
categories.videoDesc: Video understanding models running in the browser.

subcategories.classificationDesc: Assigns a label to a span of text — sentiment, topic, intent or policy flags. Encoder models in the 60–130 MB range cover most of it, and they run on WebAssembly without a GPU, which makes classification the cheapest browser AI task to ship.
subcategories.nerDesc: Extracts people, places, organisations and other spans from free text, returning character offsets rather than a rewritten string. Token classification is sensitive to tokenizer mismatches, so the exact weights and tokenizer revision matter more here than raw model size.
subcategories.translationDesc: Translates between language pairs in the browser, which keeps the source text on the device. Bilingual models stay small; the multilingual ones carry every pair in one file, so download size grows fast and some weights are licensed for non-commercial use only.
subcategories.summarizationDesc: Compresses a document into a shorter abstract. Encoder-decoder models load two graphs plus a KV cache, so peak memory is roughly double a classifier of the same parameter count, and long inputs hit the context limit before they hit the memory limit.
subcategories.chatDesc: General-purpose instruction-following models served from the page itself. Browser-side chat is bounded by WebGPU memory: 1–3B models at 4-bit fit comfortably in about 1–2 GB, while 7–8B builds need a discrete GPU and a multi-gigabyte first load that the browser must cache.
subcategories.structured-outputDesc: Constrains a language model to emit JSON, a schema or a grammar instead of prose. Most of the work is in the decoding loop rather than in the weights, so check whether the browser runtime actually exposes logit biasing or grammar support before planning around it.
subcategories.codeDesc: Code completion and code explanation models. They are ordinary decoder LLMs with a code-heavy training mix, so the browser constraints are the same as chat, while licensing differs more: several permissive-looking code models ship under their own community terms.
subcategories.embeddingDesc: Turns text into a fixed-length vector for retrieval, clustering or deduplication. These are the smallest useful models in the catalog — 30–130 MB quantised — and the vectors never leave the device, which is why local RAG usually starts here.
subcategories.rerankerDesc: Scores a query against each candidate document as a pair, which is more accurate than comparing embeddings but costs one forward pass per candidate. In a browser that cost is the whole design constraint: rerank the top 20 from a vector search, not the whole corpus.
subcategories.semantic-searchDesc: The index and query layer around embeddings: vector stores compiled to WebAssembly, or JavaScript libraries that keep the index in memory or IndexedDB. Entries here are tools rather than weights, so the number to check is index size, not download size.
subcategories.image-classificationDesc: Labels a whole image with one or more classes. The mobile-grade backbones here are the oldest reliable browser AI workload: a few megabytes, well-tested WebGL and WebAssembly paths, and frame rates high enough to run on a video element.
subcategories.detectionDesc: Finds objects and returns boxes with class scores. Post-processing is part of the cost: non-maximum suppression and letterbox scaling usually run in JavaScript, so measured latency depends as much on that glue code as on the network itself.
subcategories.segmentationDesc: Produces a per-pixel mask instead of a box — background removal, portrait effects, cut-outs. Output resolution drives the real cost: the model may be small, but the mask upsampling and canvas compositing run on every frame.
subcategories.ocrDesc: Reads text out of images and screenshots. Browser OCR is a pipeline, not one model: detection, cropping and recognition are separate stages, and language packs are downloaded per script, so the first run for a new language is not free.
subcategories.depthDesc: Estimates a depth map from a single image. The output is relative depth unless the model is explicitly metric, so it is usable for ordering, blur and parallax effects, and not for measurement without calibration.
subcategories.image-restorationDesc: Upscaling, denoising and artefact removal. These models are convolutional and tile-based, so memory scales with the output resolution rather than the weights: a 4 MB model can still exhaust a tab on a 4K image.
subcategories.text-to-imageDesc: Generates an image from a prompt. A diffusion pipeline is several networks — text encoder, UNet, VAE — and the browser must hold all of them, so the download in this category is measured in gigabytes and WebGPU is a hard requirement.
subcategories.inpaintingDesc: Fills a masked region so the result matches its surroundings — object and watermark removal, photo repair. It needs the same pipeline as text-to-image plus a mask input, and the practical browser builds are the small dedicated models rather than the full diffusion stacks.
subcategories.asrDesc: Transcribes speech to text on the device, so the audio never leaves it. Streaming is a runtime feature rather than a model feature: the same weights can either batch 30-second windows or decode incrementally, and only the latter feels live.
subcategories.vadDesc: Decides which parts of an audio stream contain speech. It is the gate in front of a transcriber — a model of a few megabytes that decides whether the expensive one has to run at all, which is usually what makes browser transcription affordable.
subcategories.audio-classificationDesc: Labels sounds and events rather than words: alarms, music, applause, acoustic scenes. Models take a mel spectrogram, so the feature extraction window, not the weights, sets the latency floor.
subcategories.ttsDesc: Synthesises speech from text in the page. Quality tracks the vocoder and the voice pack more than the parameter count, and voices are distributed per speaker, so the download you ship is one voice rather than the whole model family.
subcategories.denoisingDesc: Removes background noise from speech, usually in a real-time call or recording path. These run frame by frame at 10–20 ms hops inside an AudioWorklet, so the metric that matters is per-frame cost, not throughput.
subcategories.source-separationDesc: Splits a mix into stems — vocals, drums, bass, other. Separation is offline work: models process long windows with large FFTs, and a four-minute track takes minutes of CPU, so plan for a progress bar rather than a live effect.
subcategories.text-to-musicDesc: Generates music or sound effects from a text prompt. Audio generation is autoregressive over acoustic tokens, so generation time scales with clip length, and several of the open weights here are licensed for non-commercial use only.
subcategories.voice-cloningDesc: Reproduces a target voice from a short reference sample. The technical entry is small, the legal and consent surface is not: the catalog records licensing, but speaker consent and local likeness rules are outside what any model card can tell you.
subcategories.vlmDesc: Takes an image and a question and answers in text. A vision-language model is a vision encoder bolted onto a decoder LLM, so the browser cost is the LLM's plus an encoder pass per image, and the small builds are the only practical ones.
subcategories.clipDesc: Embeds images and text into one shared space, which makes image search, zero-shot labelling and duplicate detection a vector comparison. Two encoders ship together, but you only load the one you query with.
subcategories.document-understandingDesc: Answers questions about a page as a layout, not as a string: forms, receipts, invoices, tables. Layout-aware models read positions alongside text, which is why they beat an OCR-then-LLM pipeline on structured documents and cost more per page.
subcategories.faceDesc: Detects faces and face landmarks from a camera stream. These are the most mature real-time browser models — single-digit megabytes, 30 fps on a laptop — and the most sensitive: a camera frame is biometric input, so default to processing it and discarding it.
subcategories.poseDesc: Tracks body keypoints per frame, for fitness, motion capture and gesture control. Accuracy, latency and model size trade off explicitly here: the lite, full and heavy variants of the same model differ by several times in both size and frame time.
subcategories.handDesc: Tracks hand and finger landmarks, the basis for gesture interfaces and sign-language work. Landmark models assume a detector ran first, so the published frame rate is for the tracking stage alone unless the entry says otherwise.
subcategories.trackingDesc: Keeps an identity attached to a detection across frames. Trackers are mostly algorithms rather than weights — association, Kalman filtering, re-identification — so the entries here are WebAssembly libraries and the thing to check is CPU cost per frame.
subcategories.video-understandingDesc: Classifies or describes a clip rather than a frame. Temporal models sample 8–32 frames and run them as a batch, so the memory spike is the frame stack, and most of the published weights here have no browser build at all.

starcoder2-3b.description: BigCode StarCoder2 — modern code LLM with permissive licensing.

deepseek-coder-1-3b.description: Compact DeepSeek Coder model for browser-side code generation.

all-minilm-l6-v2.name: all-MiniLM-L6-v2
all-minilm-l6-v2.description: Tiny but high-quality sentence embeddings for semantic search.

bge-small-en.name: BGE Small EN
bge-small-en.description: BAAI BGE small embedding model, strong on retrieval benchmarks.

ms-marco-minilm.name: MS MARCO MiniLM Cross-Encoder
ms-marco-minilm.description: Cross-encoder reranker trained on MS MARCO.

bge-reranker-base.name: BGE Reranker Base
bge-reranker-base.description: BAAI BGE reranker — strong out-of-the-box reranker.

cohere-rerank-wasm.name: Cohere Rerank (ONNX)
cohere-rerank-wasm.description: ONNX port of a Cohere-style reranker for client-side use.

hnswlib-wasm.name: hnswlib.js
hnswlib-wasm.description: HNSW ANN index compiled to WebAssembly — used to do semantic search on top of embeddings.

voyager-wasm.name: Voyager (Spotify)
voyager-wasm.description: Spotify approximate nearest-neighbor search library with Python and Java bindings. No browser WASM implementation has been verified for this entry.

lancedb-js.name: LanceDB (Node)
lancedb-js.description: Embedded vector database distributed as platform-specific native binaries for macOS, Linux and Windows. There is no WebAssembly or browser build, so it cannot run on the page — it is listed to mark that gap, not as a browser option.

yolov8n.name: YOLOv8n
yolov8n.description: Ultralytics YOLOv8 nano — fast real-time object detection in the browser.

yolov5s.name: YOLOv5s
yolov5s.description: Classic YOLOv5 small model widely ported to ONNX.

mediapipe-objectdetection.name: MediaPipe Object Detection
mediapipe-objectdetection.description: MediaPipe Tasks API — EfficientDet-Lite for object detection.

ssd-mobilenet.name: SSD MobileNet v2
ssd-mobilenet.description: MobileNetV2 backbone with SSD head, packaged for tfjs-models.

imgly-bg-removal.name: IMG.LY Background Removal
imgly-bg-removal.description: The @imgly/background-removal library with its two ISNet builds: isnet_quint8 for speed and isnet_fp16 for quality. Weights are fetched from IMG.LY’s CDN at run time, so the download is not a file in the npm package.

birefnet-lite-512.name: BiRefNet-lite 512
birefnet-lite-512.description: BiRefNet-lite at 512x512, the HD background-removal path: a dichotomous segmentation model that keeps hair and thin edges the ISNet models lose. Loaded as fp16 on WebGPU, so it falls back to nothing on devices without WebGPU fp16 support.

sam-tiny.name: SAM Tiny (ONNX)
sam-tiny.description: Segment Anything Model — quantized mobile variant for the browser.

mediapipe-selfie.name: MediaPipe Selfie Segmentation
mediapipe-selfie.description: Lightweight binary segmentation for people in close-up shots.

tesseractjs.name: Tesseract.js
tesseractjs.description: Browser/Node.js OCR library wrapping Tesseract via WebAssembly. Language data is downloaded separately; PDF pages must first be converted to images.

easy-ocr.name: EasyOCR (ONNX)
easy-ocr.description: Community ONNX port of EasyOCR for the browser.

paddle-ocr.name: PaddleOCR PP-OCRv5 Mobile
paddle-ocr.description: The PP-OCRv5 mobile detection and recognition pair run through PaddleOCR.js. Both archives are small enough to self-host, which is what removes the runtime dependency on a third-party model host.

mediapipe-text.name: MediaPipe Text Detector
mediapipe-text.description: DBNet-based text detector running entirely on-device.

midas-small.name: MiDaS v2 Small
midas-small.description: Robust monocular depth estimation for the browser.

depth-anything-small.name: Depth Anything v2 Small
depth-anything-small.description: State-of-the-art monocular depth, ported to Transformers.js.

mediapipe-depth.name: MediaPipe Objectron (depth hints)
mediapipe-depth.description: Provides 3D bounding boxes and rough depth from a single image.

sdxl-turbo.name: SDXL-Turbo
sdxl-turbo.description: Real-time distilled SDXL; runs on WebGPU with onnxruntime-web.

flux-schnell.name: FLUX.1 Schnell
flux-schnell.description: Fast FLUX diffusion model. No browser build from the model owner; weights exceed browser memory budgets.

mi-gan-watermark.name: MI-GAN (pipeline v2)
mi-gan-watermark.description: A lightweight GAN inpainting model for removing watermarks and small objects. At under 30 MB it is the practical browser default; the repository also ships a plain migan.onnx, and only the pipeline build takes the image and mask as one graph.

lama-watermark.name: LaMa (ONNX fp32)
lama-watermark.description: Resolution-robust inpainting with Fourier convolutions, which holds up on large masks where MI-GAN smears. The cost is size: the fp32 export is roughly seven times MI-GAN and runs on WebAssembly.

sdxl-inpaint.name: SDXL Inpaint
sdxl-inpaint.description: SDXL variant fine-tuned for mask-based inpainting. No ONNX build is published for the browser.

whistle.name: Whistle (Cactus Compute)
whistle.description: Cactus Compute's compact speech recognition model with a 16.9 MB quantized .cact file, running locally in the browser through the Needle WebAssembly engine. Supports seven European languages, 16 kHz mono audio up to 30 seconds per pass, word timestamps and keyword biasing.

whisper-small.name: Whisper Small (Transformers.js)
whisper-small.description: Xenova/whisper-small via Transformers.js — high-precision default; quantized encoder + merged decoder ONNX.

whisper-base.name: Whisper Base (Transformers.js)
whisper-base.description: Xenova/whisper-base via Transformers.js — balanced mode; smaller encoder/decoder footprint.

whisper-tiny-wasm.name: Whisper Tiny (WASM)
whisper-tiny-wasm.description: OpenAI Whisper Tiny compiled to WASM via whisper.cpp — fastest ASR variant in the browser.

kokoro-82m-fp32.name: Kokoro 82M v1.1 (zh/en)
kokoro-82m-fp32.description: An 82M-parameter TTS model with per-speaker voice packs, outputting 24 kHz audio. The v1.1 bilingual build is loaded as fp32 on WebAssembly, and each voice pack is fetched separately from the model repository.

piper-tts.name: Piper TTS (ONNX)
piper-tts.description: Fast on-device Piper TTS — many open voices.

silero-tts.name: Silero TTS
silero-tts.description: Compact Silero TTS models with several built-in speakers.

bark-wasm.name: Bark (small)
bark-wasm.description: Suno Bark — generative audio with non-verbal cues. No ONNX or WebAssembly build is published.

rnnoise-wasm.name: RNNoise (WASM)
rnnoise-wasm.description: Xiph.org RNNoise — real-time speech denoising in the browser.

deepfilternet.name: DeepFilterNet 3
deepfilternet.description: Full-band speech enhancement at 48 kHz, exported as a single 8 MB ONNX graph driven directly by ONNX Runtime Web. Small enough to run per frame inside an AudioWorklet, which is what a live call path needs.

facebook-denoiser.name: Facebook Denoiser (ONNX)
facebook-denoiser.description: FAIR real-time speech denoiser ported to ONNX.

htdemucs-4-stem.name: HT-Demucs (4 stems)
htdemucs-4-stem.description: Hybrid Transformer Demucs splitting a mix into drums, bass, other and vocals. The fp16 export runs on WebAssembly only: ORT’s WebGPU backend cannot partition the inverse-STFT section of this graph, so the session fails to build there.

htdemucs-6-stem.name: HT-Demucs (6 stems)
htdemucs-6-stem.description: The six-source variant, adding guitar and piano at the cost of a weaker "other" stem. Same export pipeline and the same WebAssembly-only constraint as the four-stem model.

open-unmix.name: Open-Unmix
open-unmix.description: Open-Unmix — reference open-source music source separation.

moondream2.name: Moondream 2
moondream2.description: Tiny VLM for visual question answering and captioning.

llava-1-5-7b.name: LLaVA 1.5 7B
llava-1-5-7b.description: LLaVA visual chat model. No MLC or ONNX browser build is published; listed for comparison only.

paligemma-3b.name: PaliGemma 2 3B (224)
paligemma-3b.description: Google PaliGemma 2 vision-language model with an ONNX build; strong OCR, 3B parameters.

clip-vit-base.name: CLIP ViT-B/32
clip-vit-base.description: OpenAI CLIP base model — image/text embeddings in the browser.

siglip-base.name: SigLIP Base
siglip-base.description: Google SigLIP — improved image-text similarity learning.

mobileclip.name: MobileCLIP s0
mobileclip.description: Apple’s distilled CLIP for on-device use, in the smallest of its five sizes. The published release is PyTorch; the loadable build is the ONNX export, and the image and text encoders are separate files so a query only pays for one.

layoutlmv3.name: LayoutLMv3
layoutlmv3.description: Multimodal document understanding with text + layout + image.

donut-base.name: Donut (DocVQA)
donut-base.description: OCR-free document understanding transformer, DocVQA fine-tune with a Transformers.js ONNX build.

mediapipe-facedetection.name: MediaPipe Face Detection
mediapipe-facedetection.description: BlazeFace — short-range and full-range face detection.

mediapipe-facemesh.name: MediaPipe Face Mesh
mediapipe-facemesh.description: Dense 3D face landmarks for AR / analytics.

mediapipe-pose.name: MediaPipe Pose
mediapipe-pose.description: ML-based 3D pose estimation from a single image.

movenet.name: MoveNet
movenet.description: Google MoveNet — lightning/ thunder variants for pose.

posenet.name: PoseNet
posenet.description: Classic PoseNet for single-person pose estimation.

mediapipe-hands.name: MediaPipe Hands
mediapipe-hands.description: Real-time hand landmark tracking for gesture interfaces.

mediapipe-handlandmarker.name: MediaPipe Hand Landmarker
mediapipe-handlandmarker.description: Newer Tasks API version of MediaPipe Hands.

mediapipe-holistic.name: MediaPipe Holistic
mediapipe-holistic.description: Unified pipeline that tracks face, pose and hands simultaneously.

bytetrack-wasm.name: ByteTrack (WASM)
bytetrack-wasm.description: ByteTrack tracker used together with OpenCV.js for in-browser MOT.

videoclip.name: VideoCLIP
videoclip.description: CLIP-style video-text embedding for retrieval and tagging.

videomae.name: VideoMAE
videomae.description: Masked autoencoder pre-trained for video action classification.

mediapipe-classifier.name: MediaPipe Video Classifier
mediapipe-classifier.description: On-device video action classification via the MediaPipe Tasks API.

real-esrgan.name: Real-ESRGAN x4plus (fp16)
real-esrgan.description: The x4plus super-resolution model exported to ONNX with fp16 weights, run in 128-pixel tiles so memory tracks the tile rather than the image. Delivered as two byte-for-byte parts that the browser joins before building the session.

swinir.name: Swin2SR (real-world x4)
swinir.description: The successor to SwinIR, and the one with a published ONNX export: a transformer super-resolution model trained on real-world degradation rather than clean bicubic downsampling. SwinIR itself ships no browser build.

nafnet-denoise.name: NAFNet (Denoise)
nafnet-denoise.description: NAFNet — nonlinear activation free network for image denoising in the browser.

musicgen-small.name: MusicGen Small
musicgen-small.description: Meta MusicGen small (300M) — text-conditioned music generation that runs entirely in the browser via Transformers.js.

musicgen-medium.name: MusicGen Medium (ONNX)
musicgen-medium.description: Meta MusicGen medium (1.5B) — better quality, exported to ONNX for browser-side generation.

riffusion.name: Riffusion (Stable Diffusion spectrogram)
riffusion.description: Riffusion — generates music by inpainting spectrograms with a Stable Diffusion model; runs in the browser.

openvoice.name: OpenVoice v2
openvoice.description: OpenVoice v2 — instant voice cloning with tone-color control; ONNX port runs locally.

coqui-xtts.name: Coqui XTTS v2
coqui-xtts.description: Coqui XTTS v2 — short-clone voice cloning TTS; community ONNX port runs in the browser.

vectra-wasm.name: Vectra
vectra-wasm.description: A local vector index with a browser entry point, written in plain JavaScript rather than compiled to WebAssembly. It stores and queries vectors you supply; it runs no model of its own.

gemma-2-2b-it.name: Gemma 2 2B IT
gemma-2-2b-it.description: Google Gemma 2 2B instruction-tuned — small enough to load on iOS Safari via WebLLM.

smollm2-1-7b.name: SmolLM2 1.7B Instruct
smollm2-1-7b.description: Hugging Face SmolLM2 1.7B — extremely compact instruct model for browser chat.

deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-1-5b.name: DeepSeek R1 Distill (Qwen 1.5B)
deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-1-5b.description: DeepSeek-R1 reasoning model distilled into Qwen 1.5B — runs in the browser with chain-of-thought output.

florence-2.name: Florence-2
florence-2.description: Microsoft Florence-2 — unified vision foundation model for captioning, detection, OCR and grounding in the browser.

mediapipe-pose-landmarker.description: MediaPipe Pose Landmarker — modern Tasks API successor to MediaPipe Pose, with BlazePose GHUM 3D model.

silero-vad-web.description: Browser speech-activity detection through vad-web. Outputs speech segments, not transcripts or speaker identities.

mediapipe-audio-classifier.description: Web task API for audio classification. Select a compatible model asset; task-library support does not specify the weight version or measured latency.

mediapipe-gesture-recognizer.description: Hand landmarks plus a built-in classifier for seven gestures, as one Tasks API asset.

webllm-json-mode.name: WebLLM JSON mode
webllm-json-mode.description: Grammar-constrained decoding in WebLLM: the runtime restricts sampling so the output parses as JSON.

esrgan-slim.name: ESRGAN Slim (UpscalerJS)
esrgan-slim.description: A sub-megabyte ESRGAN distillation shipped as a TensorFlow.js graph model, at 2x and 4x. It trades detail for a download two orders of magnitude smaller than a full ESRGAN export.

rmbg-1-4.name: RMBG-1.4
rmbg-1-4.description: The most-downloaded background removal model on the Hub, outputting an alpha matte rather than a binary mask. Its license is Bria’s own: free for non-commercial use, commercial use requires an agreement — read it before shipping.

modnet.name: MODNet
modnet.description: Trimap-free portrait matting in 12 MB at fp16, which is small enough to run per video frame. It assumes a person in frame: on other subjects the matte degrades rather than failing loudly.

u2netp.name: U²-Netp
u2netp.description: The pruned U²-Net at 4.4 MB — the smallest salient-object model worth shipping, and the ancestor of most background-removal pipelines. Output is a coarse saliency map, so it needs refinement for hair and thin edges.

rtdetr-v2-r18.name: RT-DETR v2 R18
rtdetr-v2-r18.description: Real-time detection transformer: it predicts a fixed set of boxes, so there is no non-maximum suppression to write in JavaScript. Apache-2.0, which is the practical difference from the YOLO family.

yolov10n.name: YOLOv10n
yolov10n.description: The NMS-free YOLO generation, at nano size. Licensed AGPL-3.0 like the rest of the Ultralytics line, which reaches the application that serves it — not only the model file.

catalog.benchmarkHelp: Compare only results with the same task, input, hardware, browser and precision. No ranking is inferred from model size.
catalog.noWeights: No standalone weights specified; choose the underlying model separately.
catalog.reviewNotice: Source review is not a browser execution test.
catalog.identityWarning: Identity unresolved — exclude from model selection until verified.
catalog.legacyWarning: Legacy description; claims about performance and browser support have not been independently verified.
catalog.methodBody: Entries include models, tools and applications. An upstream example documents a browser integration, not a test on your device. Missing versions, measurements and licenses remain unverified. Historical estimates are not benchmark results.

applications.title: Application workflows
applications.intro: Practical workflow designs with linked candidate entries. These are integration guides, not tested end-to-end applications or performance recommendations.
applications.candidates: Candidate entries — check evidence before use

meeting-notes.title: Meeting transcription and notes
meeting-notes.input: Recorded audio, or microphone audio with user permission.
meeting-notes.pipeline: Segment speech with VAD → resample audio → transcribe → optionally summarize with references to timestamps.
meeting-notes.output: Timestamped text and a separately generated draft summary.
meeting-notes.limits: VAD does not identify speakers. ASR can miss names, overlap and noisy speech. A summarizer can introduce unsupported statements. Real-time operation needs separate latency tests.
meeting-notes.example: Input: a short recording. Output shape: segments with start, end and text; a summary referencing those segments. This is an interface example, not a measured result.
meeting-notes.checks: Check language, sample rate, long-recording memory use and whether any selected demo uploads audio.

document-qa.title: Local document questions
document-qa.input: Text documents or PDF pages; scanned pages require rasterization and OCR.
document-qa.pipeline: Parse/OCR → chunk with page IDs → embed → retrieve → optionally rerank → generate an answer with source excerpts.
document-qa.output: An answer with page references and the retrieved passages.
document-qa.limits: Retrieval can miss relevant pages. Embedding models do not generate answers. Tesseract.js itself does not accept PDF files. The complete workflow has not been tested here.
document-qa.example: Input: a document and a question. Output shape: answer, source page numbers and excerpts. Return an explicit no-evidence result when retrieval is insufficient.
document-qa.checks: Use the same embedding model and preprocessing for indexing and queries; check context length and test citation accuracy.

product-cutout.title: Product background removal
product-cutout.input: A product image with a clearly visible foreground.
product-cutout.pipeline: Decode and resize → foreground segmentation → refine edges → compose an alpha channel → export PNG.
product-cutout.output: An image with transparency; retain the original for comparison.
product-cutout.limits: Hair, glass, shadows and reflective products are difficult cases. Person-only segmentation is not general product segmentation. The unresolved HD entry is excluded from these candidates.
product-cutout.example: Input: a single product photo. Expected output format: PNG with an alpha channel. Compare edge crops against the original before accepting it.
product-cutout.checks: Verify the exact weight license and test edge quality, resolution and memory on representative product photos.

offline-translation.title: Offline text translation
offline-translation.input: Source text plus explicit source and target languages.
offline-translation.pipeline: Choose a compatible language pair → download and cache all assets → split text → translate → restore paragraph order.
offline-translation.output: Translated text aligned with the source paragraphs.
offline-translation.limits: Offline use requires a successful prior asset download and persistent cache. Some model pairs are one-directional. NLLB-200 distilled 600M has a non-commercial weight license.
offline-translation.example: Input: one paragraph with source=en and target=zh. Output format: a translated paragraph. Verify names and numbers independently.
offline-translation.checks: Test airplane-mode reload, cache eviction, long paragraphs and both translation directions.

live-captions.title: Live captions and on-screen translation
live-captions.input: Microphone or tab audio with user permission, processed in short windows.
live-captions.pipeline: Gate the stream with VAD → buffer a window → transcribe incrementally → translate the finalised segment.
live-captions.output: A rolling caption line plus finalised segments, each optionally paired with a translation.
live-captions.limits: Partial hypotheses change as more audio arrives, so captions rewrite themselves. Translation runs on finalised text only, which adds a visible delay on top of transcription. Bilingual models cover one direction per download.
live-captions.example: Input: live audio and a target language. Output shape: {partial, final[], translation[]}. The interface must tolerate a final segment replacing the partial text it already displayed.
live-captions.checks: Measure end-to-end delay on the target device, decide what happens when a window overruns, and confirm the translation license permits your use.

voice-assistant.title: Voice in, voice out assistant
voice-assistant.input: A microphone utterance, ended by silence detection or a push-to-talk control.
voice-assistant.pipeline: Transcribe the utterance → send the text to a local chat model → speak the reply with a TTS voice.
voice-assistant.output: A transcript, a text reply and synthesised audio, none of which leaves the device.
voice-assistant.limits: Three models are resident at once, so this is the heaviest workflow in the catalog: plan for the sum of their download sizes and peak memory. First-token latency of the chat model dominates the perceived response time.
voice-assistant.example: Input: one spoken turn. Output shape: {transcript, reply, audio}. Keep the chat history in the page so the second turn does not reload the model.
voice-assistant.checks: Check that the device has enough memory for all three models, cache weights after the first load, and provide a visible way to stop playback.

screenshot-to-data.title: Screenshot or receipt to structured data
screenshot-to-data.input: A screenshot, photo or scanned page containing a form, receipt or table.
screenshot-to-data.pipeline: OCR the page for text and positions, or send it to a layout-aware or vision-language model → constrain the model to a schema → validate the fields.
screenshot-to-data.output: A record whose fields map to your schema, with the source crop kept for review.
screenshot-to-data.limits: An OCR-then-LLM pipeline loses layout, and a layout-aware model costs more per page. Constrained decoding needs runtime support for grammars or logit biasing; without it, a schema is a prompt and not a guarantee.
screenshot-to-data.example: Input: an image and a field list. Output shape: {fields, confidence, crop}. Reject the record rather than guessing when a required field is missing.
screenshot-to-data.checks: Validate every field against your own rules, keep the image crop for a human to check, and test on the worst scans you actually receive.

inbox-triage.title: On-device message triage
inbox-triage.input: A batch of messages, tickets or comments already stored locally.
inbox-triage.pipeline: Classify each message → extract names, organisations and dates → embed the text → index the vectors for similar-case lookup.
inbox-triage.output: A label and score per message, extracted entity spans, and a nearest-neighbour list of similar past items.
inbox-triage.limits: Classifiers reflect their training data, so a moderation label is a signal and not a decision. Entity extraction returns offsets without resolving duplicates or aliases. The index must be rebuilt whenever the embedding model changes.
inbox-triage.example: Input: a message list. Output shape: {label, score, entities[], similar[]}. Route low-confidence items to a person rather than to a default bucket.
inbox-triage.checks: Measure the false-positive rate on your own data, keep the index and the model version together, and never make an irreversible decision from a single score.

image-search.title: Search your own image library
image-search.input: A local image folder or an in-page gallery, plus a text or image query.
image-search.pipeline: Embed every image once with a shared image-text model → store the vectors → embed the query → rank by similarity, optionally filtering by a classifier label first.
image-search.output: Ranked image results with similarity scores, and optional class labels as filters.
image-search.limits: Indexing cost is paid once per image and is the bulk of the work; queries are cheap. Scores are relative, so there is no absolute threshold for "a match", and the two encoders must come from the same model.
image-search.example: Input: a query string. Output shape: {results[{id, score}], took}. Show the score so a weak match does not look like a confident one.
image-search.checks: Persist vectors with the model name and revision, re-index after any model change, and test queries that should return nothing.

photo-cleanup.title: Photo cleanup and object removal
photo-cleanup.input: A single photo, plus either a user-drawn mask or boxes from a detector.
photo-cleanup.pipeline: Detect candidate objects → turn a box into a mask → inpaint the masked region → optionally upscale the result, using a depth map for depth-aware blur.
photo-cleanup.output: An edited image, the mask that produced it, and the original kept for comparison.
photo-cleanup.limits: Inpainting invents content, so the result is plausible rather than true, and removing a watermark may still be a licensing or legal question. Memory scales with output resolution, not with model size: a few megabytes of weights can still exhaust a tab on a 4K image.
photo-cleanup.example: Input: an image and a mask. Output shape: {image, mask, steps[]}. Keep every step reversible so the user can undo one stage without redoing the pipeline.
photo-cleanup.checks: Test at the largest resolution you accept, tile large images, and keep the original bytes until the user saves.

gesture-controls.title: Camera gesture and posture controls
gesture-controls.input: A camera stream, with explicit permission and a visible indicator while it is on.
gesture-controls.pipeline: Run a landmark model per frame → smooth the landmarks over time → map a held pose to an action → keep identities stable with a tracker when several people are in frame.
gesture-controls.output: Per-frame landmarks and debounced action events.
gesture-controls.limits: Camera frames are biometric input: process them in the page and discard them. Landmark models assume a detector ran first, so a published frame rate usually covers the tracking stage alone, and single-frame jitter must be smoothed before it becomes an action.
gesture-controls.example: Input: a video element. Output shape: {landmarks[], gesture, heldMs}. Require a pose to be held before firing, so a passing hand does not trigger anything.
gesture-controls.checks: Keep frames off the network, degrade gracefully when the frame rate drops, and offer a keyboard path for every gesture action.

studio-audio.title: Recording cleanup and stem split
studio-audio.input: A recorded track or a live capture; separation needs the whole file.
studio-audio.pipeline: Denoise speech frame by frame in an AudioWorklet → for a mix, split it into stems offline → optionally re-voice a narration track from a consented reference sample.
studio-audio.output: A cleaned track, separate stems as audio buffers, and any re-voiced take as a new file.
studio-audio.limits: Denoising is real-time per frame; separation is not — a four-minute track takes minutes of CPU, so it needs a progress bar rather than a live preview. Voice cloning carries a consent and likeness question that no model card answers.
studio-audio.example: Input: an audio file. Output shape: {cleaned, stems{vocals, drums, bass, other}, progress}. Run separation in a worker so the page stays responsive.
studio-audio.checks: Measure per-frame cost inside the worklet, keep separation off the main thread, and record who consented to a cloned voice before you ship it.

creative-drafts.title: Draft art and sound on the device
creative-drafts.input: A text prompt, plus a seed when a repeatable result matters.
creative-drafts.pipeline: Load the diffusion pipeline once → generate a small image at few steps → generate a short audio clip from a second prompt → keep both as drafts tied to their seed.
creative-drafts.output: Draft images and short audio clips, each with the prompt and seed that produced it.
creative-drafts.limits: This is the heaviest download category in the catalog: a diffusion pipeline is several networks and is measured in gigabytes, so WebGPU is a hard requirement. Audio generation time scales with clip length, and several open weights here are non-commercial only.
creative-drafts.example: Input: {prompt, seed, steps}. Output shape: {image, audio, prompt, seed}. Store the seed with the output or the draft cannot be reproduced.
creative-drafts.checks: Detect WebGPU before offering the feature, cache the weights after the first load, and check each weight license before publishing anything generated.

code-helper.title: In-page code assistant
code-helper.input: The current buffer, the cursor position and a short span of surrounding context.
code-helper.pipeline: Keep a code model resident → send a prefix and suffix for completion, or the selection for an explanation → stream tokens into the editor → stop on the first line that leaves the requested scope.
code-helper.output: A streamed completion or explanation, inserted only when the user accepts it.
code-helper.limits: Browser-side context windows are small, so whole-repository questions are out of scope; the model sees what you send and nothing else. Licensing varies more than in other categories: several permissive-looking code models ship under their own community terms.
code-helper.example: Input: {prefix, suffix, intent}. Output shape: {completion, tokens, stopped}. Never apply a completion without an explicit accept step.
code-helper.checks: Measure first-token latency on the target device, cap the context you send, and confirm the model license covers generated code in your product.

video-highlights.title: Clip tagging and highlight selection
video-highlights.input: A local video file; frames and audio are read through the page, not uploaded.
video-highlights.pipeline: Sample frames on a fixed stride → classify or describe each sampled window → keep identities across frames with a tracker → use audio events such as applause as a second signal.
video-highlights.output: Time ranges with labels and scores, ready to be cut or reviewed.
video-highlights.limits: Temporal models batch 8–32 frames, so the memory spike is the frame stack rather than the weights, and most published video weights have no browser build at all. A fixed stride misses events shorter than the stride.
video-highlights.example: Input: {file, strideMs}. Output shape: {ranges[{start, end, label, score}]}. Report the stride alongside the ranges so the resolution of the result is visible.
video-highlights.checks: Check that a browser build exists before planning around a model, decode in a worker, and verify the ranges against a few clips by hand.

methodology.title: How this catalog is verified
methodology.intro: Every entry mixes facts from different sources with very different weight. This page says which is which, so a reader can tell a measured number from a claim and a gap from an omission.
methodology.evidenceLead: The one thing a catalog of browser models has to be honest about is whether anyone has actually run the model in a browser.

evidenceItems.title: Browser support unverified
evidenceItems.body: Nobody has confirmed this entry runs in a browser. It is listed so its gaps are visible, not as a recommendation.

evidenceItems.title: Upstream browser example
evidenceItems.body: The project itself documents a browser integration — a usage snippet in its model card, its own web guide, or a published browser build that this catalog links to as a demo. That is a working path, not a measurement on your device.

evidenceItems.title: Tested on this site
evidenceItems.body: Measured here, with date, browser, OS, hardware, runtime version, precision and input recorded alongside the number. No entry carries this status yet.

fieldsItems.title: Download size
fieldsItems.body: The exact bytes of the weight files for that precision, read from the host that serves them. A pipeline sums its components; tokenizer and config files add under 2 MB on top.

fieldsItems.title: Historical estimate
fieldsItems.body: A size carried over from an earlier version of this catalog. Labelled as unverified wherever it appears, and replaced as soon as a real file listing exists.

fieldsItems.title: Code and weight license
fieldsItems.body: Declared by the package that ships the code and by the repository that ships the weights. A format conversion inherits its base model’s license, and that base repository is listed as a source. Blank means no source states it.

fieldsItems.title: Legacy license label
fieldsItems.body: A single license field kept from earlier records. It is never treated as verified code or weight licensing, because it does not say which of the two it described.

fieldsItems.title: Runtime version
fieldsItems.body: The current release of the runtime these records were reviewed against, read from its registry. It is not a compatibility guarantee for other versions.

fieldsItems.title: Peak memory and measurements
fieldsItems.body: Empty unless measured. Model size is not a proxy for memory use, and no ranking is inferred from it.

methodology.notClaimedTitle: What this catalog does not claim
notClaimedItems: That an entry is suitable for your use case, device or jurisdiction.
That a documented example will reproduce on your hardware or browser.
That a license summary is legal advice; read the license the source links to.
That the absence of a field means zero — it means unverified.
methodology.reviewBody: Each source carries the date it was reviewed, and pages report the latest of those dates rather than a build timestamp, so a deploy never looks like a content change. An entry whose identity is in doubt is marked unresolved and should be excluded from model selection until it is corrected rather than quietly deleted.
